w10_P4_001564: A technician on a lab bench is tallying the total energy delivered to a test rig, and the very last entry she adds to the tally is a fixed 26 J contributed by a pre-loaded spring. Just before that entry, she had multiplied a running total by 12, because the rig fires 12 identical cycles. That running total was itself 6 times the energy of motion of a single sliding cart, since the rig carries 6 such carts. Each cart has a mass of 27 kg and slides at a speed in metres per second equal to the largest whole number that divides both 363 and 346 without remainder. What is the final energy in the tally, in J?
w10_P4_001566: The net force a tugboat crew finally logs is 4 N less than an intermediate reading taken during the trial. That intermediate reading was 5 N more than the combined push of 10 identical thrusters acting together. Each thruster on its own accelerates a test block of mass 37,000 g at a rate in m/s² equal to the smaller of the two values of x for which x² - 5x + 4 = 0. What force did the crew log, in N?
w10_P4_001574: A test sled of mass 32,000 g rides a factory rail and is driven with an acceleration whose value in m/s² equals the area under the curve y = 4x² + 7x between x = 0 and x = 2. The rail's data logger reports the driving force required for this in kN. The engineer then adds a 23 kN preload reading to that value. Next she subtracts 8 kN for a calibration offset and a further 10 kN for a brake correction. What is the engineer's final figure, in kN?
w10_P4_001576: A winch on a dockside test rig pulls a 200,000 g steel block with an acceleration in m/s² equal to the smaller root of x² - 7x + 12 = 0. Three such winches pull the block together, and their combined pull is recorded in kN. A 24 kN opposing tension acts along the same line, and the rig's log defines the net force as the winches' combined pull minus this tension, with the winch direction taken as positive. The test bay is kept at 18 °C throughout the trial. Five identical rigs run at once, so the log multiplies that net force by 5. What net force does the log report, in kN?
w10_P4_001579: An electric go-kart's energy ledger over a 9-lap run is 9 times its single-lap balance. The single-lap balance is defined as the kart's energy of motion, expressed in kJ, minus the 14 kJ that its braking resistors absorb each lap, so it can be negative. The kart, of mass 60,000 g, reaches a speed in m/s equal to 10 times the larger solution of x² - 3x + 2 = 0. What is the 9-lap ledger value, in kJ?
w10_P4_001580: A 17 kg drone test pod on an outdoor launch rail reaches a speed in m/s numerically equal to the area under the curve y = 2x² + 4x from x = 0 to x = 4. Its energy of motion at that speed, less the 17 J lost to bearing friction during the run, is counted as the useful energy per run. The ambient wind speed along the rail was logged as 3.5 m/s. Two pods are launched per session and the crew runs 3 sessions, so the total useful energy is the per-run value multiplied by 2 and then by 3. Express that total in kJ.
w10_P4_001581: The final figure in a warehouse conveyor report is expressed in kJ and represents the combined energy of motion of 10 identical crates riding the belt at the same time. The report obtains it by converting the combined energy from J to kJ. Each crate has a mass of 57 kg. The belt speed in m/s is twice the greatest common divisor of 57 and 252. What is the reported total, in kJ?
w10_P4_001585: A rail-yard shunting test uses a trolley of mass 175,000 g. The trolley is accelerated at a rate in m/s² equal to the number of ways to choose 2 wheels for inspection from a set of 12. The resulting pushing force is recorded in kN. Eight trolleys are pushed simultaneously, so the recorded value is multiplied by 8, and then 3 kN of coupling drag is subtracted. What is the final force, in kN?
w10_P4_001588: A workshop crane log records, in kN, the final total thrust produced by a pair of actuator sets working together. That total is twice the output of one set. Each set is itself made of 2 identical actuators, so a set's output is twice that of a single actuator. A single actuator accelerates a 49 kg counterweight at a rate in m/s² equal to the smaller root of x² - 5x + 6 = 0. What total thrust does the log record, in kN?
w10_P4_001595: The final entry in a tow-test log is a net force in kN, obtained by taking a measured pull, subtracting the 9 kN of resistance from the anchored chain, and then adding a 2 kN tailwind assist, with the direction of the pull taken as positive. The measured pull is the force needed to accelerate a 178 kg sled at a rate in m/s² equal to the larger root of x² - 9x + 14 = 0, converted to kN. The sled's tow rope was 15 m long. What net force appears in the log, in kN?
w10_P4_001596: A 130 kg electric test chassis sits on a dynamometer bench. Its controller sets an acceleration in m/s² found by taking the smaller root of x² - 3x + 2 = 0, multiplying it by 11, and then subtracting 4. Each of the chassis's 12 wheel motors is rated to supply on its own the force required for this acceleration, and the bench records the sum of the 12 ratings. Finally, a 21 N spring preload is added to that sum. What is the final force, in N?
w10_P4_001604: The total energy in a bicycle-fleet report, in kJ, is 2 times a shift total. The shift total is 8 times a route total. The route total is 10 times the energy of motion of a single rider-and-bike, after that energy has been converted from J to kJ. The rider and bike together have a mass of 55,000 g and roll at a speed in m/s equal to the smaller root of x² - 9x + 20 = 0. What is the fleet total, in kJ?
w10_P4_001609: A 105 kg pallet on an automated warehouse shuttle is accelerated at a rate in m/s² equal to the area under the curve y = 3x² + 3x between x = 2 and x = 3. The shuttle's drive must provide the force for this acceleration, less the 6 N that a passive roller contributes. The shuttle's track is 48 m long. The controller converts the drive force to kN and multiplies it by 12 to size the drive for a 12-shuttle system. What is the sized drive force, in kN?
w10_P4_001610: The final value in a bridge-jack report is in kN and is found by adding 20 kN of dead-load allowance to a subtotal. That subtotal is 7 kN more than a net force expressed in kN. The net force is a jack's push minus 27 N of seal friction. The jack pushes a 123 kg beam with an acceleration in m/s² equal to the greatest common divisor of 120 and 55. The beam is 6.5 m long. What is the final value in the report, in kN?
w10_P4_001611: A 76 kg cargo sled on a mine rail is accelerated at a rate in m/s² found by taking the area under the curve y = 1·x² + 8x between x = 0 and x = 3 and subtracting 25. The rail engine must supply the force for this acceleration, and the log converts that force to kN. The sled's cargo was loaded at 14 °C. A 20 kN safety margin is then added. What is the final force in the log, in kN?
w10_P4_001613: A shipyard's final tally is a force in kN equal to 12 times a per-bay figure. The per-bay figure is 8 times a single-jack figure, which is expressed in kN. The single-jack figure is 30 N more than the force required to push a 134,000 g plate at an acceleration in m/s² equal to the smaller root of x² - 3x + 2 = 0. The plate is 2.4 m wide. What is the shipyard's final tally, in kN?
w10_P4_001618: The figure a race-team engineer finally quotes, in kJ, is 11 times a per-car figure. The per-car figure is the car's energy of motion plus 11 J of stored flywheel energy, converted to kJ. The car has a mass of 36,000 g. Its speed in m/s is 2 times the sum of 3 and 13. What figure does the engineer quote, in kJ?
w10_P4_001620: A 24 kg robot-vacuum prototype glides across a test floor at a speed in m/s equal to the smaller root of x² - 3x + 2 = 0. Its energy of motion is measured, and 10 such prototypes run at once, so the lab multiplies by 10. The test floor is 7 m long. The combined value is converted to kJ and then multiplied by 10 again for the 10 test sessions. What is the final energy, in kJ?
w10_P4_001623: A 31,000 g sled moves at a speed in m/s obtained by taking the area under y = 4x² + 4x from x = 0 to x = 3 and subtracting 18. Its energy of motion is converted to kJ. The sled's brakes are rated to dump 23 kJ, and the log records the energy of motion minus that rating, which is negative when the brakes have spare capacity. The sled's track sits at an altitude of 450 m. What value does the log record, in kJ?
w10_P4_001624: The value a lift engineer reports, in kN, is 10 times a single-cable figure. The single-cable figure is a net force expressed in kN. That net force is 29 N less than the force needed to accelerate a 182,000 g counterweight at a rate in m/s² equal to the greatest common divisor of 327 and 183. What value does the engineer report, in kN?
w10_P4_001644: A delivery-drone fleet report ends with a total in kJ that is 9 times a per-drone figure. The per-drone figure is 21 kJ of battery reserve plus a flight quantity expressed in kJ. That flight quantity is 17 J more than the energy of motion of one drone. Each drone has a mass of 8,000 g and cruises at a speed in m/s equal to the larger root of x² - 9x + 14 = 0. What total does the report give, in kJ?
w10_P4_001645: A 21,000 g test projectile on a catapult range leaves the rail at a speed in m/s equal to the area under the curve y = 3x² + 6x between x = 3 and x = 4. Its energy of motion, less 7 J lost to the release latch, is the launch energy. The range is 120 m long. The crew fires 3 shots per round, so the round energy is 3 times the launch energy, and 23 J of sensor overhead is subtracted from each round's figure. Five rounds are fired, and the total is 5 times the per-round figure. What is the total, in J?
w10_P4_001664: A 50,000 g cart on a lab bench moves at a speed in m/s equal to the area under y = 2x² + 5x from x = 0 to x = 1. A data logger records its energy of motion. It then applies four corrections in order: it adds 14 J, adds 7 J, subtracts 12 J, and adds 7 J. The bench is 1.8 m long. What is the corrected energy, in J?
w10_P4_001680: A 69,000 g crate on a loading ramp is accelerated at a rate in m/s² equal to the area under y = 5x² + 3x from x = 1 to x = 2. The force required for this is increased by 16 N of belt tension, and the result is converted to kN. A 12 kN structural allowance is then added. The total is multiplied by 7 for the 7 ramps in the facility. What is the final figure, in kN?
w10_P4_001689: A 68,000 g dummy on a crash sled is accelerated at a rate in m/s² equal to 7 times the smaller root of x² - 7x + 12 = 0. The restraining force required for this is converted to kN. Then 26 kN of frame preload is added. Six sleds run simultaneously, so the total is 6 times that sum. What is the total, in kN?
